rationale: The valuation leg is identical to the archive's best-performing "Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield," but the conditioner is genuinely re-specified from a balance-sheet stock ratio to a flow-based cash-runway coverage measure, which is a defensible economic distinction worth one test, though the expected incremental information is modest.

This is essentially "Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield" with an identical second leg and interest merely subtracted from the numerator — a cosmetic tweak on a channel the archive has already probed repeatedly (After-Interest Claim Yield, Net Current Liquidity Surplus, Core Margin Floor), so it is unlikely to be informative about anything new.

Wrapping IND_ADJ around the dp/at term of the earlier "Low-Depreciation Cash Operating Yield" is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and it is implausible that sector demeaning of one SUMRANK component explains a fmb_tstat of −1.041 coexisting with a +4.74 alpha t-stat — that disagreement points to composition/weighting or size-tilt issues, not industry effects.

Conditioning cheap post-depreciation operating income on industry-adjusted asset turnover introduces a genuinely new (DuPont-efficiency) conditioner not yet in the archive and is internally consistent, though value×turnover interactions are close to well-documented profitability-value territory and the conditioner is a low-frequency, slow-moving variable.

The parent "Cash-Burn Revenue Overprice" already produced a fmb_tstat of 0.02 with only a modest negative alpha, and swapping oibdp/sale for oiadp/at inside the same SUMRANK is a minor accounting substitution rather than a diagnosis of why the cross-sectional evidence collapsed.

Piling a fourth term onto an already-failed composite via nested SUMRANK (which silently assigns half weight to the profitability term and a quarter each to the others) is kitchen-sink construction, and the added rising-interest × weak-profitability leg duplicates the archive's "Rising Interest Cost Profit Trap."
